problem:
A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x$ meters, its velocity is $v\,m/s,$ the magnitude of its acceleration is $6x\,{m/s}^{2},$ and the acceleration is directed toward $O.$
If $P$ has velocity $4\,m/s$ when its displacement is $2\,m,$ find the values of $x$ for which $P$ is instantaneously at rest.

activity_context.topic_title: Determining Properties of Objects Described as Functions of Displacement

feedback.problem:
A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x$ meters, its velocity is $v\,m/s,$ the magnitude of its acceleration is $2x\,{m/s}^{2},$ and the acceleration is directed toward $O.$
If $P$ has velocity $4\,m/s$ when its displacement is $1\,m,$ find the values of $x$ for which $P$ is instantaneously at rest.
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094290/assets/4b08d915d0adf8bf603070aa96bde1edf0cfb392d9be5f9bd4786897a6c943fa.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ has magnitude $2x\,{m/s}^{2}$ and is directed *toward* $O,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=-2x.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=-2x.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (-2x)\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=-{x}^{2}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=4\,m/s$ when $x=1\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =-{x}^{2}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(4)^{2} & =-(1)^{2}+C \\ C & =8+1 \\ C & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=9-{x}^{2}.
$$

Finally, the particle is instantaneously at rest when $v(x)=0\,m/s.$ We find the displacement of the particle when instantaneously at rest by substituting $v=0$ in the equation above and solving for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =9-{x}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{2}(0)^{2} & =9-{x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2} & =9 \\ x & =\pm 3\,m.\end{aligned}
$$
